examples.en: I compared the two hotels and then chose one.
Don't compare yourself with other people.
I compared prices online and bought it.

examples.ko: 휴대폰 두 개를 놓고 비교를 했어요.
examples.en: I put two phones side by side and compared them.

examples.ko: 친구하고 비교를 하면 기분이 안 좋아요.
examples.en: I feel bad when I compare myself with my friends.

explain: ‘A를 B와 비교하다’처럼 ‘와/과’를 써요. ‘비교’ 뒤에 ‘하다’를 붙이면 동사가 돼요.
explain_en: It works like A를 B와 비교하다, with 와/과. Add 하다 to 비교 and it becomes a verb.

examples.en: My main criterion for choosing a place to stay is location.
Every company has different rules for vacation days.
The passing standard for the exam is seventy points.

examples.ko: 무료 배달 기준이 얼마예요? — 이만 원부터예요.
examples.en: What's the minimum for free delivery? — It starts from 20,000 won.
Check the hiring criteria on the website.

explain: ‘N을/를 기준으로’는 ‘N을 표준으로 해서’라는 뜻이에요: 가격을 기준으로 골라요.

explain_en: N을/를 기준으로 means “using N as the standard,” as in 가격을 기준으로 골라요 (I choose based on price).

examples.ko: 도서관 운영 시간은 저녁 열 시까지예요.
examples.en: The library's opening hours are until 10 p.m.
The opening hours are shorter on weekends.
What are the museum's opening hours?
Please come within the opening hours.
The opening hours are different on public holidays.

explain: 가게나 식당은 ‘영업시간’, 도서관이나 박물관은 ‘운영 시간’이라고 많이 말해요.
explain_en: Shops and restaurants are often said to have 영업시간, while libraries and museums have 운영 시간.

examples.ko: 회의실 이용료는 한 시간에 오천 원이에요.
examples.en: The meeting room fee is 5,000 won per hour.

examples.ko: 헬스장 이용료가 한 달에 오만 원이에요.
examples.en: The gym fee is 50,000 won a month.
The pool fee is 10,000 won per day.
There is no fee to use this service.
The usage fee is cash only.

explain: ‘-료’는 ‘값, 돈’을 뜻하는 끝말이에요: 이용료, 주차료, 입장료, 수업료.
explain_en: The ending -료 means a fee: 이용료, 주차료 (parking), 입장료 (admission), 수업료 (tuition).

examples.en: This store has branches all over the country.
It'll rain nationwide tomorrow.
This song is popular all over the country.
I want to travel around the whole country.
Our team won at the national competition.

explain: ‘전’(全)은 ‘모두’라는 뜻이에요. 전국, 전체, 전부에 같은 ‘전’이 있어요.
explain_en: 전 (全) means “all.” The same 전 is in 전국, 전체 and 전부.

examples.en: Domestic flights are expensive, so I take the train.
I took a domestic flight from Gimpo Airport.
I booked a domestic flight to Jeju Island.

examples.ko: 국내선은 한 시간 전에 공항에 도착하면 돼요.
examples.en: For a domestic flight, it's enough to arrive at the airport an hour before.

examples.ko: 국내선 탑승구가 어디예요? — 이 층 오른쪽에 있어요.
examples.en: Where is the domestic flight gate? — It's on the second floor, to the right.

explain: 반대말은 ‘국제선’(international flight)이에요. 공항 안내판에도 둘이 따로 적혀 있어요.

dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 국내선 비행장은 국제선 비행장에 비해 규모가 작은 것이 일반적이다.
dict_examples.en: Domestic airports are generally smaller than international airports.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: The opposite is 국제선 (international flight). Airport signs list the two separately.

examples.en: I rented a public bike and rode it to school.
Public libraries don't charge a fee.
The public restroom is inside the station.
I use the public Wi-Fi on the subway.
The public parking lot is cheap, so it's busy.

explain: 공공은 보통 명사 앞에 붙여서 써요. 공공 시설, 공공 도서관처럼 모두가 쓰는 것을 말해요. 반대말은 ‘개인’이에요.
explain_en: 공공 usually goes right before a noun, as in 공공 시설 (public facility) or 공공 도서관. It means something everyone can use. The opposite is 개인 (private, personal).

examples.en: Don't talk loudly on the phone in public places.
You can't smoke in public places.
A bus stop is a public place too.
The subway is a public place. Please talk quietly.
In public places, I wear earphones to listen to music.

explain: 공원이나 도서관처럼 모두가 쓰는 곳이 공공장소예요. 우리 집은 공공장소가 아니에요. 공공 ‘public’ + 장소 ‘place’예요.

dict_examples.ko: 몇몇 젊은이들이 공원 한쪽에서 공공장소라는 것도 잊은 채 시끄럽게 떠들어 대고 있다.
dict_examples.en: A few young people at one side of the park are chattering noisily, forgetting it is a public place.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 병원, 학교, 지하철역과 같은 공공장소 곳곳에 ‘금연’이라는 게시문이 붙어 있었다.
dict_examples.en: No-smoking notices were posted all over public places such as hospitals, schools, and subway stations.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: A park or a library is a 공공장소, a place everyone uses. Your own home is not. It is 공공 (public) + 장소 (place).

examples.en: I caught a cold yesterday.
When I catch a cold, I drink warm water.

examples.ko: 동생이 감기에 걸려서 학교에 못 가요.
examples.en: My younger sibling has a cold and can't go to school.
Be careful not to catch a cold.

examples.ko: 날씨가 갑자기 추워져서 감기에 걸리는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: The weather suddenly got cold, so many people are catching colds.

explain: ‘감기에 걸리다’는 한 덩어리로 외우세요. ‘감기를 걸리다’라고 하지 않아요. 다 나으면 ‘감기가 나았어요’라고 하고, 감기를 조심하라고 할 때는 ‘감기 조심하세요’라고 인사해요.
explain_en: Memorize '감기에 걸리다' as one chunk; don't say '감기를 걸리다'. When you recover, say '감기가 나았어요'. To tell someone to take care, Koreans say '감기 조심하세요' as a greeting.

examples.en: I caught a cold last week.
Watch out for colds in winter.

examples.ko: 감기가 심해요. 오늘은 병원에 갈 거예요.
examples.en: My cold is bad. I'll go to the hospital today.

examples.ko: 동생이 감기예요. 그래서 오늘 학교에 안 가요.
examples.en: My younger brother has a cold. So he isn't going to school today.
My throat hurts. Is it a cold?

explain: ‘감기’는 가벼운 cold예요. 열이 많이 나고 심하게 아픈 flu는 ‘독감’이라고 해요.

dict_examples.ko: 이불을 걷어차고 자더니 감기에 걸렸나 보다.
dict_examples.en: He slept kicking off the blanket, so he must have caught a cold.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 감기 is the common cold. A strong flu with a high fever is called 독감.
